topik.nama: 1. Grammar: Passive Voice and Reported Speech

nota.t: The passive voice (be + past participle) focuses on the action: The bridge was built in 1990. Reported speech shifts tenses back and changes pronouns and time words: 'I am tired,' he said → He said he was tired.

t: be + past participle: The room is cleaned. The letter was written.
Use by + doer only when it matters.
Tense moves back: am → was, will → would, can → could.
Commands: told me to …; questions: asked me where I lived.

nota.t: Modals express ability (can), permission (may), obligation (must), advice (should) and possibility (might). Connectors link ideas: and, but, because, so, although, however, therefore.
Prefixes change meaning (un-, dis-, mis-, re-, pre-) and suffixes change word class (-ness, -ment, -ful, -less, -able): happy → unhappy → happiness.
Reading for detail: read the question first, underline key words, then scan the text for names, numbers, dates and places.
Inference: use clues in the text such as actions, words and feelings, together with your own knowledge, to understand what is suggested but not stated.
For literature, study the theme, characters, setting, plot and literary devices, and support your answer with evidence from the text.

t: must (rule), should (advice), might (possibility), may (permission), could (past ability), needn't (not necessary), mustn't (not allowed).
un-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, dis- make opposites.
Read the questions first, scan for key words, check details carefully.

nota.t: Collocations are words that naturally go together: make a decision, do homework, heavy rain, take a photo, strong coffee.
Idioms have meanings that are not literal: break the ice (start a conversation), under the weather (unwell), a piece of cake (very easy), once in a blue moon (rarely).

t: make a mistake, do homework, take a photo, pay attention.
a piece of cake = very easy; once in a blue moon = very rarely.
